P1.evidence: Setter notes were read back well and the prospect visibly warmed to it — 'I talked with Kim. You spoke with him a few days ago. He briefed me in on your situation. So you've been training since 2009.' But no four-part frame was set and no frame agreement was sought; the call went straight from rapport into training history. The open question arrived late and in a narrower form at 00:07:43 — 'what's the gap? Like, what's, what's missing?' — rather than an open 'what are you looking for help with'.

P2.evidence: Height and weight came out ('I'm like 5'10"... I'm like 183') but age was never asked. Occupation was volunteered unprompted — 'I'm a teacher, and it just happened that my schedule worked out really well' — and never asked, so it scores a miss. Health conditions, injuries, chronic pain and movement limitations were never raised at any point in 49 minutes, on a call selling loaded ballistic kettlebell work to a 40-something with a decade of CrossFit volume behind him. Sleep and daily energy were never asked. Training week and results were covered thoroughly, and diet was caught late — 'I remember that I didn't ask you about the nutrition.'

P3.evidence: The strongest phase of the call by a distance. The rep refused to accept the aesthetic answer and pushed the why hard — 'Let me ask you this. Why? What is it for?' and then 'So let me ask you then, again, what's the why?' — which produced a genuine admission: 'I know that my why is not good enough... I don't have the why.' He then bridged to family, drew out the two children, and reflected it back cleanly: 'So it's not about... It's number on the scale, and it's not about the aesthetics anymore.' The prospect confirmed and re-anchored on athleticism and playing with his kids.

P4.evidence: A full history was drawn out — the affiliate closing, the bodybuilding detour, the second affiliate, Street Parking, Thunder Bro, Josh Bridges, Jeff Nippard — and the rep summarised it as 'it's not your first rodeo'. He asked 'But you didn't stick with anything for a longer period?' which is a weaker form of why it did not stick, and got the prospect to name the gap himself: one-on-one coaching, 'that's what's been missing'. The scripted 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' was never asked.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind was run. The two-year question, the willing-to-settle question, the why-not and the line-in-the-sand were all absent. The rep went from the reflected-back goal at 00:20:57 into the three pillars and then straight into price. This is the phase that decided the call: with no cost of inaction established, the prospect had nothing weighing against a $6,000 number he could not fund, and he defaulted to sleeping on it.

P6.evidence: The belief check was run properly and answered strongly — 'Do you actually believe that this is achievable for you?' / 'Yes, I do. I believe it and I know it.' The all-in check was started and abandoned mid-sentence at 00:31:41 — 'if you had this right training in place, proper nutrition and accountability and guidance from Trevor, do you actually feel that that would get you to' — and the rep cut himself off and moved into the six-month logistics and price without ever completing it or getting the answer. He therefore presented on a belief yes rather than a commitment yes, which is precisely what the phase exists to prevent.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies, but no payment was collected — the call ended with 'Sleep on it' and a next-day booking. Steps 2 to 4 were unreachable with no sale. The only link sent was a financing application to a third-party processor, sent before any agreement to proceed.

objection_plays.detail: Ran nearly complete. Isolated first — 'let's put finances just for a second on a sideline, do you personally feel that this can get you to your goals'; used the should-I/how-do-I reframe almost verbatim — 'we're just in a, not in a should I do it place, or we are in a more, how can I actually make it possible'; asked permission for the money conversation — 'would you be open to have a conversation about finances too?'; then ran the full financial picture in order: cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, and crypto/stocks/investments. The 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up' move was also run. Only gap: he never returned to close after building the picture, he handed over a financing link and let the call end on the prospect's hard stop.

Two of the six moves ran. The money-aside belief check ran and landed, and the obstacle preview ran — 'when you talk to her, actually, like, what do you feel potential obstacles might be?' The rep did not ask whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and less in pain, did not test whether this genuinely needs her input versus asking permission to bet on himself, did not use the not-a-joint-decision-like-buying-a-house frame, and did not offer the deposit-plus-refund fallback. He accepted the spouse consult and booked a call instead.

The trigger was explicit — 'I'm not going to just decide right now. Anyway, I want to sleep on it'. The rep ran the can-it-get-you-there and why-do-you-feel-it-can pair well ('Why do you feel that it can actually?' producing a strong answer about previous one-on-one coaching) and asked the blocker question 'So what's coming up?' twice. He then abandoned the play: no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no identity move, no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. He closed by agreeing to the delay — 'Sleep on it. But I think that this is the right solution.'

Timing surfaced twice, as upcoming senior-year expenses and as waiting for the union contract and pay rise to land. The rep ran one move — start now rather than wait: 'you can actually just start and don't wait for the um for the bump with the with the project' — but did not run the things-never-slow-down frame, the cost-of-delay frame, or the only-thing-you-can-control-is-right-now close. Notably the P5 consequence frame that would have powered this was never built.

Script gap: cross-border currency. The prospect raised the exchange rate as a distinct value objection — 'my Canadian dollars are not as much as the U S dollar' — and the effective price for him is about CAD 8,300. There is no scripted play for FX-inflated pricing, and the rep's only handling was to help compute the larger Canadian figure, which strengthened the objection rather than answering it. Worth adding to the playbook given how much of this corpus is non-US.

Script gap: a cheap alternative that genuinely worked. The prospect ran Street Parking at '20 bucks a month' for about two years and stacked several other low-cost programmes successfully. This is the same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call — Objection C assumes capacity to pay is the blocker, not perceived value against a functioning low-cost substitute. The rep never addressed the 300x price ratio at all.

notes: Excellent discovery, no consequence frame, and a close attempted on a belief yes rather than a commitment yes. The single highest-leverage fix is P5 — the rep built a strong family why and then never made inaction cost anything, so a prospect with real intent had no reason not to defer. Second fix: complete the P6b question instead of cutting it off to talk price. Third: baseline is thin in a way that matters clinically — no injury, health or pain question was asked in 49 minutes before recommending loaded ballistic training to a long-time CrossFitter.
